battle.name: 第一次西西里戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前480年夏，迦太基將軍哈米爾卡率遠征軍在西西里島北岸希梅拉上岸；敘拉古的革隆與阿克拉加斯的提隆聯軍在城北平原迎敵。迦太基海軍先在港外覆滅，陸戰中哈米爾卡大敗，僅以數艘船隻逃回。卡面月牙劍在埃及退出戰役數百年，西西里重步兵握的仍是直身短劍、矛與大盾。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 第一次西西里戰爭是公元前480年迦太基與西西里島希臘城邦聯軍之間的一場衝突，戰線落在島的北岸與東岸，最終以希梅拉（Himera，今泰爾米尼伊梅雷塞）城外的平原會戰定出勝負。迦太基一方是北非迦太基城邦在西地中海的殖民體系：北非本土的徵召兵與雇傭兵、腓尼基式造船技術撐起的船隊、已經在島西立足的殖民地與盟邦（莫提亞、帕諾爾莫斯、索盧斯），再加上與之結盟的塞列斯提人與塞加斯塔人聚落，共同組成這支遠征軍，由哈米爾卡以將軍身份總攬。聯軍一方是西西里的希臘城邦聯盟：以敘拉古的革隆為首，核心是敘拉古的城邦軍與受雇的希臘雇傭兵；阿克拉加斯（Akragas）由提隆率步兵與騎兵赴援；希梅拉、卡拉尼亞、卡馬利納等小城也各有分遣；此外還有自伊斯特摩斯戰線折返的弗基與卡里亞水手與士兵，以及西原住民西卡利人與西拉尼人，用作輕裝兵與騎兵補充。兩邊的指揮體系並不相同：迦太基以一名將軍全權統轄全軍，再分派各路分遣，戰後由迦太基公民議事會裁斷功過；希臘聯軍則靠各城邦領袖的個人權威拼合而成，戰前有共同敵人作為黏合劑，戰後的戰利品分配與政治算帳卻要各城自行協商。
countriesEn: The First Sicilian War was a conflict in 480 BC between Carthage and a league of the Greek city-states of Sicily, fought along the north and east coasts of the island and decided at last in the open plain outside Himera, the modern Termini Imerese. On the Carthaginian side stood the western Mediterranean system built by the North African city of Carthage: men levied in the homeland together with mercenaries, a fleet kept in the Phoenician shipbuilding tradition, the colonies and allies already established in the west of the island (Motya, Panormos and Solous), and the Segestan and Sicanian communities that had thrown in their lot with them. Together these made up the expedition, which was led as a whole by Hamilcar in the capacity of general. The other side was the league of the Sicilian Greek cities: at its head Syracuse under Gelon, with the citizen force of the city and Greek mercenaries in its pay; Akragas (Akragas) sending foot and horse under Theron; detachments from the smaller communities of Himera, Carania and Camarina; and, brought back from the Isthmus line, Phocians and Carians with their ships and their men, together with Sicels and Sicani from the indigenous population, used as skirmishers and light horse. The two command systems were not alike. Carthage's general held full authority over the whole force and delegated it to separate columns, and after the fighting the Carthaginian citizen assembly passed judgement on what had been done. The Greek league rested on the personal authority of the individual city leaders, held together before the war by a common enemy, but left to settle the accounts and divide the spoils among themselves afterwards.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物分屬兩邊。聯軍這邊居首的是敘拉古的僭主革隆（Gelon），公元前485至478年在位，治下把敘拉古推成西地中海最強的希臘城邦；他這次以「伊斯特摩斯方面的希臘海軍總指揮」身分被推舉為聯軍主帥，卻把主力調回西西里對付哈米爾卡，戰後仍保住敘拉古的霸位，日後由其弟希耶羅一世接位。阿克拉加斯的提隆（Theron，公元前485至472年在位）是另一支柱，他調來五千步兵與二百騎兵，在戰線左翼作戰；同行的還有阿克拉加斯的將領與城邦軍。援軍方面，自伊斯特摩斯戰線折返的弗基與卡里亞水手在西西里海戰中毀掉迦太基艦隊，是這場戰爭的轉折點之一；西原住民西卡利人與西拉尼人則以輕騎與散兵身分參戰，在關鍵時刻追擊潰兵。迦太基這邊，將軍哈米爾卡是全軍統帥，也是後來漢尼拔·巴爾卡之父（史料或記他為漢諾之子）；第比烏斯記他為全軍主將、哈諾為一翼指揮，希羅多德則記海軍統帥為漢諾之子哈米爾卡、陸軍統帥為哈米爾卡之子哈諾。哈諾在陸戰失利後帶著殘部逃回迦太基，被公民議事會當眾處死；哈米爾卡則僅以一艘三列槳船與少數隨行逃出海上。聯軍這邊還有兩個值得記的名字：西西里北岸的埃格斯特人（塞加斯塔人）首領，正是他們到雅典與斯巴達求援，才把這場戰爭拉進希臘人的世界；以及呂基翁的希耶羅二世之前的阿納克西拉（Anaxilas），他早於戰役二十八年，與提隆、革隆一起在希梅拉舊城之外重建了希梅拉城，把流亡的希梅拉人安置下來，也因此在戰役爆發時，雙方都不願讓這座城落入對方之手。戰後數十年，敘拉古的狄奧尼修斯一世又會在同一片島上與迦太基開戰，而那位哈米爾卡會在公元前388年陣亡於島上——距希梅拉之戰九十二年。
peopleEn: The named figures of the war fall on two sides. At the head of the league stands Gelon of Syracuse, tyrant from 485 to 478 BC, who in his time made Syracuse the strongest Greek city in the western Mediterranean; he had been chosen as commander of the Greek fleet at the Isthmus, but turned his main force back into Sicily against Hamilcar, and afterwards kept his position at Syracuse, to be succeeded by his brother Hiero I. Theron of Akragas, tyrant from 485 to 472 BC, was the other pillar, bringing five thousand foot and two hundred horse and fighting on the left of the line, with Akragantine commanders and the citizen force of his city alongside. Among the reinforcements were the Phocians and Carians brought back from the Isthmus line, whose work in the naval battle off Therma destroyed the Carthaginian fleet and so made a turning point of the whole war; and the Sicels and Sicani of the indigenous population, who served as light horse and skirmishers and who were decisive in pursuing the broken enemy. On the Carthaginian side, the general Hamilcar commanded the expedition as a whole, and was the father of Hannibal Barca (some sources make him the son of Hanno); Diodorus gives him as commander in chief with Hanno leading a wing, while Herodotus names Hamilcar son of Hanno as commander of the fleet and Hanno son of Hamilcar as commander of the land force. Hanno led the remnant back to Carthage after the land battle and was torn to pieces by the citizen assembly in the open; Hamilcar escaped by sea with a single trireme and a few companions. Two further names belong to the Greek side. The chiefs of the Egestans, the Segestans of the north Sicilian coast, were the men who carried their appeal to Athens and to Sparta and so dragged the war into the Greek world; and Anaxilas of Rhegium, who twenty-eight years before the battle, together with Theron and Gelon, had refounded the city of Himera outside its old site and settled the exiled Himeraeans there, which is why neither side was willing to let the city fall to the other. Decades later, Dionysius I of Syracuse would wage war against Carthage on the same island, and that Hamilcar would be killed there in 388 BC, ninety-two years after Himera.
kits: 先把卡面上這把兵器講清楚：埃及月牙劍（khopesh）是青銅質、單刃、刃口開在凸面、整體彎如新月的近身兵器，砍入人身或盾牌之後不必回抽再揮。它在古王朝時期就已出現，到新王國時期讓位給背脊平直的鐮形劍（khesebet 與 sekhem），在希臘化時代更退居祭祀與儀仗之列；換句話說，到了公元前480年，這件形制在埃及本土早已離開戰場數百年，在西地中海的戰場上更不曾出現。它值得放進希梅拉的裝備表，理由有兩層。第一，它屬於「單刃弧形、順勢劈砍」這條技術路線的祖型，而這條路線在希臘世界仍有活著的後代：科佩斯（kopis），一種前段略彎、刃口朝外、握柄偏前端的輕型單刃劍，西部希臘的輕裝兵與標槍兵普遍使用；希梅拉戰場上真正握在希臘人手上的近身兵器則是兩面直身的鐵短劍（xiphos），配七尺至八尺的長矛（dory）與直徑近一米的圓盾（aspis），重步兵另有青銅或亞麻的胸甲（linothorax）、護脛與科林斯式或雅典式頭盔；敘拉古與阿克拉加斯的工坊與埃爾巴、希西里的礦冶業，供應著上等鐵料，這一帶的希臘重裝兵裝備水準在西希臘世界居於前列。第二，迦太基一方的裝備與希臘人同源而略偏輕：布甲與亞麻疊層胸甲、青銅頭盔（多有護頰）、圓盾、投槍與短劍；其短劍的柄形在愛琴海與西地中海考古中屢見，屬於同一個武器文化圈。兩邊真正吃重的是騎兵：敘拉古與阿克拉加斯都養出成軍的騎兵隊與供應馬匹的牧場，聯軍還有西卡利與西拉尼的輕騎；哈米爾卡也帶來北非的騎兵。軍隊的輸送全靠船隊，這本是一場海運遠征，糧秣、攻城器與補充兵員都從海上來；希梅拉城外的會戰是野戰，沒有大型攻城器投入，而同年提隆圍攻塞利努斯時才用到圍城木架與封鎖。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card has to be explained first. The khopesh is a close-combat blade of bronze, single-edged, with the edge on the convex side and the whole blade curved like a new moon, so that once it has been driven into a body or a shield it does not have to be pulled back out before the next stroke. It appears already in the Old Kingdom, gave way in the New Kingdom to the straight-backed sickle sword, the khopesh-like khesebet and sekhem, and by the Hellenistic age had retreated into the sphere of sacrifice and parade. In other words, by 480 BC this form had left the Egyptian battlefield several centuries earlier and had never appeared on a battlefield in the western Mediterranean at all. It is worth placing in the equipment table of Himera for two reasons. First, it is the ancestor type of one line of technique, the single-edged curved cut that follows the stroke, and that line had a living descendant in the Greek world: the kopis, a light sword with a slightly forward curve, an edge on the outside and a grip set toward the front, carried by light infantry and peltasts throughout the western Greek world. The weapon actually in the hands of the Greeks at Himera was the two-edged straight iron shortsword, the xiphos, with a spear of seven or eight feet, the dory, and a round shield of nearly a metre's diameter, the aspis. Their heavy infantry also had bronze or linen cuirasses, the linothorax, greaves, and Corinthian or Attic helmets; the workshops of Syracuse and Akragas, working iron from the Elban and Sicilian sources, put the equipment of the Sicilian hoplites among the best in the western Greek world. Second, the Carthaginian equipment was of the same cultural stock but somewhat lighter: cloth and layered linen body armour, bronze helmets, most of them with cheek pieces, round shields, javelins and short swords, the hilt form of which turns up again and again in the archaeology of the Aegean and the western Mediterranean. What really counted on both sides was the cavalry: Syracuse and Akragas maintained formed bodies of horse and the pastures that supplied them, and the league added the light horse of the Sicels and Sicani; Hamilcar in turn brought North African cavalry. The movement of the army was the work of the fleet, for this was a campaign carried by sea, and grain, siege matériel and replacements all came by water. The battle outside Himera was a battle in the open, with no great siege engines committed to it, although in the same year Theron's siege of Selinus called for timber batters and a blockade.
tactics: 整場戰爭可以分成海陸兩段來看，兩段的關鍵都與地形有關。海戰在希梅拉的港市忒耳瑪外海舉行：哈米爾卡的迦太基艦隊排成戰列，弗基與卡里亞人駕船靠上，以撞角與接舷作戰，把迦太基海軍在港內外打得全毀；海軍既失，遠征軍就失去了海上補給線與撤退的船。陸戰的部署由地勢決定：希梅拉城北是一片開闊的濱海平原，一條塞爾穆斯河橫貫其間，河道在夏季可以涉渡；聯軍占據城北的高地，把平原對岸讓給迦太基軍營，營地緊靠海灣，艦隊原可停泊其間作補給與撤退之用。哈米爾卡在營中列陣，以中軍與哈諾的一翼對著聯軍正面；希臘聯軍這邊，革隆與敘拉古騎兵在右翼，提隆與阿克拉加斯騎兵在左翼，中間是希梅拉與其他西西里城邦的步兵，並夾雜西卡利人的輕裝步卒。開戰前一夜，哈米爾卡企圖夜襲希臘營壘，卻被巡哨發現，希臘人倉卒結陣以待，迦太基軍在黑暗中失去行列，損失了一部分兵力。接著是全天最關鍵的騎兵交鋒：迦太基騎兵衝擊敘拉古騎兵，阿克拉加斯騎兵一度被衝散，隨後回身再戰，聯軍的輕裝步兵與投槍手在兩翼不斷侵擾，迦太基騎兵終於崩潰，朝營地方向逃竄；西卡利人的輕騎追上去，在河床與營門一帶砍殺大批潰兵。主戰在隨後展開：希臘重步兵結成長陣推進，迦太基中軍一度頂住，但兩翼騎兵崩潰之後，側翼被聯軍輕兵纏住，整條陣線隨之折斷，迦太基步兵被推回自己的營地。營地這時成了陷阱：入口被自家潰兵堵死，聯軍的輕騎與步兵趕到，在河邊與營門外大量殺傷，泗水與踐踏造成更多人馬的損失；哈米爾卡與少數人趁海軍未及的最後時機奪船而走。戰後聯軍同時分兵圍攻塞利努斯，把城中的財貨大部運回阿克拉加斯。
tacticsEn: The whole war can be read in two stages, a naval and a land one, and in both of them the terrain was decisive. The naval action was fought off Therma, the harbour town of Himera: the Carthaginian fleet of Hamilcar was drawn up in line, while the Phocians and Carians closed in under sail, working with rams and boarding, and destroyed the Carthaginian ships inside and outside the harbour. With the navy gone, the expedition lost both its sea line of supply and the ships by which to retreat. The land deployment was settled by the ground. North of the town of Himera lies an open coastal plain crossed by the river Selsius, fordable in the summer months. The league took the high ground north of the town and left the plain across the river to the Carthaginian camp, which stood close to the bay so that the fleet might lie there and feed the army or carry it away. Hamilcar deployed with his main body in the centre and Hanno on one wing against the front of the league; on the Greek side Gelon and the Syracusan horse were on the right, Theron and the Agrigentine horse on the left, the foot of Himera and the other Sicilian cities in the centre, with Sicel light infantry mixed among them. On the night before the action Hamilcar attempted a surprise attack on the Greek camp; the watch caught him, the Greeks closed up in a line, and the Carthaginians lost their order in the darkness and a part of their strength with it. The decisive phase of the day was then the cavalry: the Carthaginian horse charged the Syracusan, the Agrigentine cavalry was scattered and then returned to the fight, the light infantry and the javelin men of the league kept up the pressure on both flanks, and the Carthaginian horse broke and ran for the camp, where the light horse of the Sicels overtook them and cut down great numbers at the river bed and at the camp gate. The main engagement followed: the Greek heavy infantry advanced in a long line, the Carthaginian centre held for a time, but once the cavalry on both wings had gone and the flanks were being worn down by the light troops, the line folded and the Carthaginian foot was pushed back into its own camp. The camp then became a trap: its entrance was blocked by the soldiers of its own army who had fled there, the light horse and foot of the league came up, and a great many were killed at the water's edge and outside the gate, more still were drowned or trampled. Hamilcar and a few men got away in time to seize boats, before the sea was closed to them. After the battle the league simultaneously turned on Selinus and carried the wealth of the city back to Akragas.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是古代作家自己說的。希羅多德《歷史》第七卷記革隆率二千騎兵與一萬五千步兵、乘一百艘三列槳船與五十艘運輸船前往伊斯特摩斯；同書記哈諾統率的陸軍為四萬步兵與三千騎兵，並記哈米爾卡最後僅以一艘三列槳船逃出。提隆從阿克拉加斯調來五千步兵與二百騎兵，是第比烏斯《歷史文庫》第十一卷的數字；同一卷給迦太基方面的總兵力記為以數十萬計，後世學者多認為這一數字被上古典作家系統性誇大。戰損方面，第比烏斯所記為希臘方面數百人陣亡、迦太基方面以萬計，同樣被視為可疑的說法。戰爭年份沒有爭議：公元前480年；希梅拉會戰的月份兩部古史都未固定，通行說法是夏季，且與溫泉關、薩拉米斯戰役同一年，迦太基遠征軍於是年春季出航。第二類是編制與地理。革隆的僭主統治期為公元前485至478年，提隆為公元前485至472年；希梅拉城在公元前488年由希耶羅、提隆與阿納克西拉在舊址之外重建；希梅拉今屬泰爾米尼伊梅雷塞，位於北緯38.08度、東經13.23度，會戰平原在城北，臨近塞爾穆斯河與通往帕諾爾莫斯的沿海大道；聯軍陣地取自希梅拉城外的制高點，迦太基營地則在河對岸的海濱平地上。第三類是現代推估：聯軍作戰兵力當在步兵一萬上下加上約二千騎兵的量級，迦太基一方在數萬人上下而非數十萬；史料之所以差距懸殊，部分原因在於古史家慣於把「全島兵力的總和」當作一場會戰的實際到場人數。時間跨度上，希梅拉之戰到公元前474年的庫邁海戰是西西里戰爭的最後一役，到公元前388年哈米爾卡陣亡在西西里，距希梅拉九十二年；到公元前264年第一次布匿戰爭因美西拿而爆發，距希梅拉二百一十六年。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the ancient writers say of themselves. Herodotus, Book 7, has Gelon taking two thousand horsemen and fifteen thousand foot to the Isthmus with a hundred triremes and fifty transports; the same book gives the land force under Hanno as forty thousand foot and three thousand horse, and has Hamilcar escaping on a single trireme. Theron's contribution of five thousand foot and two hundred horse from Akragas is Diodorus Siculus, Library of History, Book 11; the same book puts the total strength on the Carthaginian side at a number in the hundreds of thousands, a figure most modern scholars regard as systematically inflated by the classical historians. For losses, Diodorus gives a few hundred Greeks killed against thousands upon the Carthaginian side, and that too is treated as suspect. The year of the war admits no dispute: 480 BC. Neither ancient history fixes the month of the battle at Himera; the usual placing is in the summer, in the same year as Thermopylae and Salamis, the expedition having sailed in the spring of that year. The second class is organisational and geographical. Gelon's tyranny ran from 485 to 478 BC and Theron's from 485 to 472 BC; the city of Himera was refounded outside its old site in 488 BC by Gelon, Theron and Anaxilas; Himera is the modern Termini Imerese, at 38.08 degrees north and 13.23 degrees east, the plain of the battle lying north of the town, near the river Selsius and the coastal road to Panormos, the league taking its ground from the heights outside Himera while the Carthaginian camp stood on the coastal plain across the river. The third class is modern estimate: the league's field force on the order of ten thousand foot with about two thousand horse, and the Carthaginian force in the tens of thousands rather than the hundreds of thousands. The gap in the sources is in part explained by the habit of ancient writers treating the sum of the island's total manpower as the number actually present in one battle. In span of time, the last round of the Sicilian war was the naval battle of Cumae in 474 BC, and Hamilcar was killed in Sicily in 388 BC, ninety-two years after Himera; the First Punic War broke out over Messana in 264 BC, two hundred and sixteen years after Himera.
cause: 打起來的原因由外到內疊了四層。最外一層是突發的導火索：公元前480年，迦太基趁波斯大軍壓境之際出兵西西里，攻下北岸的塞加斯塔（埃格斯特）城，把這座長期保持獨立、拒絕臣服於任何一方的城邦收為己有；城邦的居民向雅典與斯巴達求援，雅典派出二十艘三列槳船，斯巴達與科林斯卻以不在伯羅奔尼撒作戰為由推辭，最後只有敘拉古與阿克拉加斯這兩個強者真正接下了戰書。第二層是全希臘的戰局：薛西斯大舉西征，希臘城邦的兵力正向伊斯特摩斯與薩拉米斯集中，迦太基在這個節骨眼上同波斯議和（第比烏斯第十一卷），等於站到了希臘人的對面；西西里人擔心戰火燒到島上，也擔心自己不在大戰中分擔，便把希梅拉的戰場當成自己的戰場。第三層是西地中海的結構性矛盾：迦太基推動西西里西部的殖民事業，控制伊利亞人的城塞與埃里克斯的維納斯聖地壟斷，同時在糧食、琥珀與金屬的路上同希臘殖民地正面相撞；莫提亞、索盧斯與迦太基有血緣上的聯繫，埃格斯特人與塞利努斯人則長期拒絕希臘人的佔領，雙方都明白這一帶的歸屬會改變整個島的力量對比。第四層是個人與政治的算計：革隆需要一場全島皆知的大勝來鞏固敘拉古的霸權，提隆則早就覬覦西部的穀物與城邦財富；早在公元前488年三人合力在希梅拉舊城外重建新城時，這種對西部的爭取就已開始。技術層面的原因同樣具體：迦太基遠征軍以雇傭兵為主力，指揮關係鬆散，一旦在陣前被正面擊敗，陣營與海岸線之間的退路便會立刻變成陷阱；而聯軍雖然號令不統一，卻共享同一個敵人、同一個目標與同一批能打的騎兵。
causeEn: The causes stack from the outside in, in four layers. The outermost is the occasion. In 480 BC, while the great Persian army was pressing into Greece, Carthage moved in Sicily and took the Segestan city of Egesta, a town long independent and unwilling to submit to anyone; its people appealed to Athens and to Sparta, Athens sent twenty triremes, and Sparta and Corinth declined on the ground that they were not fighting in the Peloponnese, so that in the end only two strong cities, Syracuse and Akragas, took up the challenge. The second layer is the situation of the whole Greek world: Xerxes was campaigning in the west, the forces of the Greek cities were concentrating on the Isthmus and at Salamis, and Carthage concluded a treaty with Persia in that same moment, as Diodorus records, which put it on the other side of the line; the Sicilian Greeks feared that the war would reach the island, and feared still more to be left out of the great struggle, so they made the field of Himera their own. The third layer is the structural contradiction of the western Mediterranean: Carthage pushed its colonial work in western Sicily, held the Elymian strongholds and the sanctuary of Venus at Eryx, and collided head on with the Greek colonies over grain, amber and metal; Motya and Solous were bound to Carthage by ties of blood, while the Egestans and the Selinuntines had long refused Greek occupation, and both sides understood that the ownership of this coast would change the balance of the whole island. The fourth layer is personal and political calculation: Gelon needed a victory known across the island to hold his position at Syracuse, and Theron had long coveted the grain and the wealth of the western towns; that competition for the west had begun as early as 488 BC, when the three of them refounded Himera outside its old site. The technical reasons are just as concrete. The Carthaginian expedition was made up in its bulk of mercenaries, and its chain of command was loose; once it was beaten in the open, the ground between the camp and the shoreline became a trap at once. The league, for all its divided command, shared one enemy, one purpose and one body of serviceable horse.
impact: 希梅拉的結果改變了西西里島往後兩百年的格局。第一，迦太基未能在島上取得立足之地：莫提亞、帕諾爾莫斯、索盧斯三座西部城池與埃格斯特人這一類盟友仍舊存在，但島的東岸與北岸完整留在希臘城邦手中，這套希臘與腓尼基的界線一直維持到公元前264年美西拿的危機。第二，敘拉古因此成為西希臘世界的霸主：革隆在薩拉米斯與普拉提亞兩戰之後的西西里遠征，使他同時握有希臘同盟海軍的指揮權與西西里的全勝，敘拉古隨即在西西里、義大利南部與希臘本土之間插手，與迦太基的爭奪從島內延伸到海上。希羅多德記下的一件事至今仍是耐人尋味的枝節：聯軍內部曾懷疑革隆同波斯暗中妥協，這份戒心令雅典人對敘拉古的忠誠一直不放心。第三，戰爭的戰利品改變了島內的力量：塞利努斯的城財被阿克拉加斯吞併，提隆的西進政策因此得以上手，阿克拉加斯在數年之後達到鼎盛；同一時期希梅拉也獲得喘息，新城在戰後容納了大量來自被毀城邦的人。第四，軍事上的教訓被後世反覆引述：決定希梅拉的不是步兵的數量，而是騎兵的較量與營地的位置，一支把營地設在海岸而把退路交給已經覆沒的艦隊的軍隊，註定在陣線一動時便無處可退。第五，這場戰爭是迦太基一系的重要心理節點：哈米爾卡是漢尼拔·巴爾卡之父，父親在西西里留下的敗績，兒子在二十餘年後仍被迦太基人記得；美西拿危機之所以會在公元前264年把迦太基拖入西西里戰爭，前提正是這次遠征失敗後，島上兩種力量被長期凍結在同一個僵局之中。
impactEn: The result of Himera shaped the western Mediterranean for the two centuries that followed. First, Carthage failed to gain a footing on the island: Motya, Panormos and Solous and allies such as the Egestans remained, but the east and north coasts of Sicily stayed entire in the hands of the Greek cities, and that line between Greek and Phoenician Sicily was to hold until the crisis of Messana in 264 BC. Second, Syracuse became the leading power of the western Greek world: Gelon's Sicilian campaign, fought alongside Salamis and Plataea, left him holding at once the command of the allied Greek fleet and a complete victory in Sicily, and Syracuse began to interfere in Sicily, in southern Italy and in the Greek mainland alike, so that the quarrel with Carthage passed from the island to the sea. A detail Herodotus preserves has stayed puzzling: the suspicion in several Mediterranean cities that Gelon was in secret concert with the Persians, out of which the Athenians' mistrust of Syracuse grew. Third, the spoils of the war rearranged the balance inside the island. The wealth of Selinus was absorbed by Akragas, Theron's western policy got its way, and Akragas reached the height of its power within a few years; in the same period Himera drew breath and the new city received many of the people of the destroyed towns. Fourth, the military lesson was quoted again and again afterwards: what decided Himera was not the number of foot but the trial of horse and the position of the camp, and an army that pitched its camp on the shore and entrusted its retreat to a fleet already destroyed was doomed the moment its line moved. Fifth, the war was a turning point in the self-consciousness of the Carthaginian house: Hamilcar was the father of Hannibal Barca, and the defeat in Sicily was remembered by the Carthaginians for a generation and more after his son; and the crisis at Messana that dragged Carthage into the Sicilian wars in 264 BC had as its precondition precisely the long frozen standoff between two powers in Sicily that followed this failure.
result: 公元前480年夏，戰爭以兩次打擊收場：先是希梅拉港外的海戰，迦太基艦隊被弗基與卡里亞人毀滅；再是城北平原的會戰，哈米爾卡的遠征軍被革隆與提隆的聯軍擊潰，營地被攻破，哈米爾卡只帶少數人奪船逃回迦太基。哈諾率殘部逃回後在公民議事會上被當場處死，第比烏斯記錄了這場處決的慘烈；希羅多德則記哈米爾卡以一艘三列槳船歸國。同一個戰役季節裡，提隆完成對塞利努斯的圍攻，島的西岸從此盡入阿克拉加斯的掌握，迦太基以希梅拉為支點西進的計畫徹底破滅。但戰爭並未因一役而終結：迦太基仍保有西部三城與對埃格斯特人的影響，雙方的角力又拖了六年，最後由敘拉古的希耶羅一世在公元前474年的庫邁海戰中擊敗由哈諾與希拉姆指揮的迦太基艦隊，戰爭才算收官，第一次西西里戰爭亦以這次海戰為其通常的終點。結果可以這樣總結：西西里島從此分成一個由敘拉古主導的希臘東半部、一個由迦太基主導的腓尼基西半部，兩者之間夾著塞利努斯、塞加斯塔、莫提亞的走廊，這條走廊在公元前三世紀變成了第一次布匿戰爭的戰場。回頭看卡面那把月牙劍，它走過的路線恰好是這場戰爭的隱喻：從古埃及的近身兵器，到新王國的儀仗，再到自己身後一千年被重新發掘的文物；它在西西里平原上真正對應的，是那些同樣彎曲、同樣單刃、同樣不必回抽的輕型單刃劍——科佩斯，它們在希臘人手裡仍然天天見血，只是已經不再叫那個埃及的名字。
resultEn: In the summer of 480 BC the war came to a close in two blows. First the naval battle off the harbour of Himera, where the Carthaginian fleet was destroyed by the Phocians and Carians; then the engagement in the plain north of the town, where Hamilcar's expedition was broken by the league of Gelon and Theron, the camp was stormed, and Hamilcar seized boats and got back to Carthage with a handful of men. Hanno brought the remnant home and was killed on the spot before the citizen assembly, in a scene Diodorus describes with some rigour; Herodotus has Hamilcar return in a single trireme. In the same campaigning season Theron completed the siege of Selinus, the west coast of the island passed for the most part into the hands of Akragas, and the Carthaginian plan of driving west from Himera was broken outright. The war did not, however, end with that one battle. Carthage kept its three western cities and its influence over the Egestans, the struggle between the two sides dragged on for six more years, and it was settled at last by Hiero I of Syracuse, who in the naval battle of Cumae in 474 BC destroyed the Carthaginian fleet commanded by Hanno and Hiram; the First Sicilian War is conventionally closed by that engagement. The result can be put this way: Sicily was divided into a Greek eastern half under the leadership of Syracuse and a Phoenician western half under Carthage, with the corridor of Selinus, Segesta and Motya lying between them, and that corridor was to become the battlefield of the First Punic War in the third century BC. Looked at from the card, the khopesh has travelled a road that is an image of the war itself: from the close-combat weapon of the Egyptian Old Kingdom, to the parade piece of the New Kingdom, to an antiquity rediscovered a thousand years after its own time. What it truly corresponds to on the Sicilian plain is the family of light single-edged swords that are also curved, also single-edged, and equally need not be withdrawn after the stroke: the kopis, still drawing blood in Greek hands, though no longer bearing the Egyptian name.
